alex: heads-up — canary (redwood-dedicated-pt1) showing tail latency regression on the kv-prefetch path after yesterday's kernel-selector change.  p95 jumped ~2.3x. anyone else seeing this?

maria: saw the alert, digging into traces now. looks like more kernel switches per request than before (more small kernels invoked).

kai: can you repro locally? getting a capture will help. try nsight run with both nvtx and osrt so we see selector + runtime handoffs.

alex: repros consistently on our perf harness. uploading a short capture in a minute. planning to run with these flags:

alex: ```
nsys profile --output=canary_kv_repro \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu --sample-interval=100us \
  --duration=20s \
  --capture-range=nvtx:kv-request-start-kv-request-end \
  --force-overwrite --max-size=4GB \
  -- python perf_harness.py --scenario=kv-prefetch --batch=8
```

maria: nice. include `--sample-window=5s` to bias toward steady-state if you want to avoid warmup noise. also put nvtx markers around the batching decision code (selector) so we can see kernel selection boundaries.

kai: example NVTX snippets:

alex: ```c
// around selector code
nvtxRangePushA("selector:decide-kernel");
choose_kernel(...);
nvtxRangePop();

// around kv lookup
nvtxRangePushA("kv-lookup");
// call into runtime that triggers kernels
call_runtime();
nvtxRangePop();
```

jun: fwiw I captured one with `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` and `--sample=none` to get exact timelines — saved a few GBs by using `--duration=12s` and `--capture-range=nvtx:prep-start:prep-end`. file attached in thread.

nsys-bot: capture finished: canary_kv_repro.qdrep (size 1.3GB) -> uploaded to /shared/profiles/4860123456-canary_kv_repro.qdrep

maria: quick look — kernel selector emits two NVTX ranges per request now, previously one. selector appears to pick a tiled-matmul kernel for short sequences which increases overhead due to extra kernel launches.

alex: do we have a baseline capture from before the selector change? want to diff timelines.

kai: yes — dug one up: 4839990000_kv_baseline.qdrep. plan: run `nsys stats` to get kernel timeline and kernel counts, then `nsys profile --stop-on-exit` to bracket warmup.

maria: command I used for quick kernel counts: `nsys profile --trace=cuda --duration=10s --output=counts qdrep` then `nsys stats counts.qdrep --report=all` (filters: kernel name, launch count, total time).

alex: result from baseline vs canary: kernel launches per request baseline=3, canary=7. median kernel time per kernel reduced slightly, but launch overhead accumulates.

jun: suggests selector heuristics are too eager to break into smaller kernels (maybe trying to optimize for peak FLOPs but ignoring launch cost). Can we force the old kernel via env var to confirm?

kai: yes — runtime supports `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=matmul_v1` for a quick A/B. try one run with that env var and compare p95.

alex: ran `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=matmul_v1` on canary — p95 returned to baseline. so selector change is likely root.

maria: next steps: 1) revert or gate selector change (canary only) 2) add a test in perf CI that counts kernel launches per request 3) add telemetry in selector to record estimated launch overhead vs compute benefit.

kai: for future captures, if you need smaller qdrep files: use `--sample=periodic` with `--sample-interval=500us` and `--sample-window=8s`, and bracket capture with NVTX around the exact region to avoid huge file sizes. also try `--gpu-metrics-reply` off if you don't need perf counters.

alex: noted. also saw some KV cache miss spikes correlated with extra kernel launches — likely cache not warming because of different kernel entry pattern. please add a KV miss-rate counter in selector tracing.

maria: added a short logging patch to record kv-hit-rate per request and NVTX-push the value (so it correlates in timeline). will push to canary later today.

jun: one more tip — if you're only interested in kernel timelines, `--trace=cuda` + `--capture-range=process:start-end` is enough; skip osrt if you want smaller files and fewer markers. but osrt helps when trying to link runtime events to kernel dispatch latency.

alex: thanks everyone. I'll open a canary rollback PR and attach the captures + nsys stats to the PR. keeping this thread as the central repro. :thumbsup:

maria: cool — if anyone else sees odd p95 after the rollback, ping here.

kai: rough checklist for future: sample vs full timeline tradeoffs, NVTX around selector, env var toggle, perf CI kernel-launch assertion, KV hit telemetry. I'll make a GH issue.

alex: added issue #1287 and linked PR. closing the loop after revert verification.

nsys-bot: FYI — existing shared captures: /shared/profiles/4839990000_kv_baseline.qdrep, /shared/profiles/4860123456-canary_kv_repro.qdrep
